content.text:
Found it — it's not the pods, it's the Service.

## Root cause: typo in the `checkout` Service selector

```
Service selector:  app.kubernetes.io/name: chekout   ← missing 'c'
Pod labels:        app.kubernetes.io/name: checkout
```

Nothing matches the selector, so `endpoints/checkout` is empty and the EndpointSlice has no addresses. Every request to `checkout.demo.svc:80` gets connection-refused/no-route even though both pods are healthy.

Evidence:
- Both `checkout` pods are `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts — you were right that pods are fine.
- I curled a pod IP directly on `10.244.0.8:8080` → **HTTP 200**. The app is serving fine.
- `endpoints/checkout` → `<none>`; `endpointslice checkout-ddxbs` → `<unset>`.

Also worth noting: the Service's `last-applied-configuration` annotation still says `"selector":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"checkout"}` — spelled correctly. So the live object drifted from what was applied; someone did a `kubectl edit`/`patch` on the running Service rather than changing the manifest. That's consistent with "fine this morning."

## Fix

One-line patch:

```bash
kubectl patch svc checkout -n demo --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"checkout"}}}'
```

Endpoints should populate immediately. I haven't applied it — say the word and I'll run it and verify endpoints come up. You'll also want the same correction in whatever manifest/IaC owns this Service, or the next apply may reintroduce drift (the annotation suggests the source of truth is already correct, in which case a plain re-apply also fixes it).

## Separate, pre-existing issue

`payments` has two pods in `CrashLoopBackOff` — 781 restarts over 2d23h. That's unrelated to the checkout selector and predates today, but if checkout calls payments you'll have a second failure waiting behind this one. Want me to dig into that next?

content.text:
DNS is ruled out. Here's the evidence.

## Support's observation is real — their conclusion isn't

They're not making it up. From a busybox/alpine debug pod, `nslookup checkout.demo.svc` genuinely returns NXDOMAIN. I reproduced it exactly.

But here's the control that settles it:

```
### busybox nslookup, kubernetes.default.svc  (a service that definitely works) ###
** server can't find kubernetes.default.svc: NXDOMAIN
** server can't find kubernetes.default.svc: NXDOMAIN

### busybox nslookup, checkout.demo.svc ###
** server can't find checkout.demo.svc: NXDOMAIN
** server can't find checkout.demo.svc: NXDOMAIN
```

`kubernetes.default.svc` is the cluster's own API service — it has healthy endpoints and works fine. It fails **identically**. So the NXDOMAIN is an artifact of busybox's `nslookup`, which mishandles the `ndots:5` search-path expansion. It is not specific to checkout and not evidence of a DNS fault.

With a real resolver, the name resolves fine:

```
getent hosts checkout.demo.svc.cluster.local
  -> 10.96.189.187        # this is what apps actually use (glibc/musl)

dig +search checkout.demo.svc            -> 10.96.189.187
dig +search checkout.demo.svc.cluster.local -> 10.96.189.187
```

CoreDNS itself is healthy: both replicas `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts, `kube-dns` service has both endpoints (`10.244.0.6`, `10.244.0.3`).

## Where the request actually dies

DNS succeeds, then the connection fails:

```
checkout.demo.svc.cluster.local  -> resolves to 10.96.189.187   ✅ DNS fine
curl http://checkout.demo.svc/   -> exit 7, connect_time 0.000  ❌ refused instantly
curl http://10.244.0.7:8080/     -> 200                          ✅ app fine
curl http://10.244.0.8:8080/     -> 200                          ✅ app fine
```

`connect_time 0.000000` with curl exit 7 is the signature of no backend: kube-proxy has no endpoint to DNAT to, so the ClusterIP rejects immediately. Not a timeout, not a resolution failure. Name → IP works; IP → pod has nothing behind it, because the selector typo (`chekout`) matches zero pods.

So the diagnosis is unchanged, and now it's positively confirmed rather than inferred: **empty endpoints from the selector typo**, not DNS.

## Worth telling support

Their debug pod's `nslookup` will keep lying to them. Suggest they use `getent hosts <name>` or `dig +search`, or test with `curl -v` — the distinction between "can't resolve" and "resolved but refused" is exactly what got misread here.

## The patch, still unapplied

```bash
kubectl patch svc checkout -n demo --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"checkout"}}}'
```

Want me to apply it? I'd then re-run the same `curl http://checkout.demo.svc/` from a pod — it should flip from exit 7 to 200, which confirms the fix against the actual reported symptom rather than just against endpoint output. And the manifest still needs the same correction so the drift doesn't come back.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# break-checkout.sh — the chapter-10 incident. Puts a one-character typo in the
# checkout Service's selector ("chekout"), so the service goes dark while every
# pod stays green: no crashloop, no warning events, nothing the installed skills
# fire on. That gap is the point — explore it with Claude, then extract the
# findings into a new skill with skill-creator.
#
#   ./demo/break-checkout.sh          # break it
#   ./demo/break-checkout.sh --fix    # restore the correct selector
#   ./demo/break-checkout.sh --test   # curl it from inside the cluster
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

case "${1:-}" in
  --fix)
    kubectl apply -f "$HERE/k8s/checkout.yaml" >/dev/null
    echo "fixed: selector restored to app.kubernetes.io/name=checkout"
    kubectl -n demo get endpoints checkout
    ;;
  --test)
    kubectl -n demo run curl-test --rm -i --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 \
      -- wget -qO- -T 3 http://checkout.demo.svc/ \
      && echo "service is UP" || echo "service is DOWN"
    ;;
  "")
    kubectl -n demo patch service checkout --type merge \
      -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"chekout"}}}' >/dev/null
    echo "broken: Service selector now says 'chekout' (endpoints will be empty)"
    kubectl -n demo get endpoints checkout
    ;;
  *)
    sed -n '2,11p' "$0"; exit 2 ;;
esac

content.text:
Fixed and verified end to end.

## What I did

```bash
kubectl patch svc checkout -n demo --type=merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"selector":{"app.kubernetes.io/name":"checkout"}}}'
```

## Verification

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `endpoints/checkout` | `<none>` | `10.244.0.7:8080, 10.244.0.8:8080` |
| EndpointSlice ready | `<unset>` | `true, true` |
| `curl checkout.demo.svc.cluster.local` | exit 7, refused | **200** |
| `curl checkout.demo.svc` (support's form) | refused | **200** |
| `curl checkout` (short name) | refused | **200** |
| From another namespace | refused | **200** |
| 30 sequential requests | — | **30/30 · 0 failures** |

`kubectl diff -f demo/k8s/checkout.yaml` returns nothing, so live state now matches the manifest — no lingering drift.

## Provenance — worth knowing

This wasn't organic. `demo/break-checkout.sh` in this repo applies that exact typo deliberately; its own header says it "puts a one-character typo in the checkout Service's selector so the service goes dark while every pod stays green." The script also ships a `--fix` that re-applies the manifest — functionally identical to my patch. If someone ran that script, the incident starts and ends there. If nobody admits to running it, that's the more interesting question.

## What to watch for

**The core failure mode: pod health and service reachability are different things.** Every readiness probe was green, zero restarts, no warning events. Nothing that alerts on pod state would ever have fired — and that's exactly why support reached for "must be DNS." A service can be 100% dark with a 100% green fleet.

**1. Alert on zero-endpoint Services.** This is the single highest-value gap. Here's a scan you can run now (currently clean):

```bash
kubectl get endpointslice -A -o json | jq -r '
  .items[] | select(.metadata.labels["kubernetes.io/service-name"]) |
  select([.endpoints[]?.conditions.ready // false] | any | not) |
  "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.labels["kubernetes.io/service-name"])"'
```

As a Prometheus rule, alert when a Service has 0 ready endpoints for >2m while its workload has ready pods — that pairing distinguishes "selector broken" from "app genuinely down."

**2. Selector typos are invisible to the API server.** Label values are free-form strings; `chekout` is perfectly valid YAML and valid Kubernetes. No schema validation will ever catch it.
